title: Generic flatness and local finite presentation over a reduced algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $Y$ is reduced: every etale scheme chart of $Y$ has local rings without nonzero nilpotents. Suppose $f$ is of finite type, meaning quasi-compact [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then there exists an open subspace $D\subseteq Y$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] whose underlying subset is dense in the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], such that $X\times_YD\to D$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No quasi-separatedness, Noetherianity, irreducibility, or quasi-compactness of $Y$ is assumed; the empty base and empty source are allowed.

source.place: Tag 06QS (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), the morphism conclusion, obtained by taking the structure sheaf in its finite-type module clause.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale atlas $V=\coprod_i V_i\to Y$ with each $V_i$ affine, using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Its components are etale over $Y$: their inclusions are open immersions, hence etale, and etale maps compose. Each $V_i$ is reduced by the hypothesis on the etale charts of $Y$. Put $X_i=X\times_YV_i$. This is an algebraic space. Since $V_i$ is quasi-compact and $f$ is quasi-compact in the stated base-change sense, $X_i$ is quasi-compact. Choose any scheme atlas of $X_i$ and apply [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] to obtain a representable surjective etale atlas $U_i\to X_i$ with $U_i$ affine. This argument uses no quasi-separatedness of $X_i$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 06QS (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), proof, scheme-atlas and affine-base reductions; only the morphism conclusion.

proof.text: The composite $g_i:U_i\to V_i$ is locally of finite type: it is a presentation diagram for $f$, with both chart maps etale, so the etale source-and-target criterion applies to this property. Here [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] supplies that locality and [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] identifies its extension with the chart meaning in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-affine-generic-flat-finite-presentation] to $g_i$, whose source and reduced target are affine. It gives a dense open $D_i\subseteq V_i$ such that $E_i=U_i\times_{V_i}D_i\to D_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. There is no need to assume that the entire atlas $V$ or the entire base $Y$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 06QS (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), proof, scheme-atlas and affine-base reductions; only the morphism conclusion.

proof.text: The composite $D_i\hookrightarrow V_i\to Y$ is representable etale. Its image is an open subspace $W_i\subseteq Y$ by [lem-a1-etale-scheme-map-open-image]. Let $D$ be the open subspace corresponding to $\bigcup_i|W_i|$, using the open-subspace correspondence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. The maps $D_i\to D$ are etale and jointly surjective: on every scheme test over $D$ their pullbacks are exactly their pullbacks over $Y$, and their point images cover $|D|$. The base changes $X\times_YD_i\to X\times_YD$ form an etale covering family. Each $E_i\to X\times_YD_i$ is the base change of the surjective etale map $U_i\to X_i$, so it is surjective etale. Consequently the composites $E_i\to X_D=X\times_YD$ are etale and jointly surjective. All these fibre products and etale base changes are covered by the two cited space fibre-product and scheme-test lemmas.

source.place: Tag 06QS (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), proof, scheme-atlas and affine-base reductions; only the morphism conclusion.

proof.text: We verify descent without assuming the charts $D_i\to D$ are quasi-compact. Let $P$ be flatness or local finite presentation, and take any presentation diagram $A\to X_D$, $B\to D$, $h:A\to B$ with $A,B$ schemes and both chart maps etale. Set $B_i=B\times_DD_i$ and $C_i=A\times_{X_D}E_i$, which are schemes by representability. The maps $C_i\to E_i$ and $B_i\to D_i$ are etale base changes of the given charts. There is a map $C_i\to B_i$ induced by its maps to $A\to B$ and $E_i\to D_i$. The square with $E_i\to D_i$ commutes. Since that last map has $P$, the scheme source-and-target lemma gives $P(C_i\to B_i)$. The family $C_i\to A$ is jointly surjective etale, and $B_i\to B$ is etale. For every $a\in A$ choose a point above it in one $C_i$; this supplies exactly the pointwise etale source-and-target test (iii) for $h$. Thus $h$ has $P$. Every presentation diagram has $P$, so [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] proves that $X_D\to D$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. This uses the pointwise locality statement, not a quasi-compact descent assertion.

source.place: Tag 06QS (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), proof, scheme-atlas and affine-base reductions; only the morphism conclusion.

proof.text: Finally let $O\subseteq|Y|$ be a nonempty open subset. Surjectivity of the atlas gives an $i$ for which the inverse image $O_i\subseteq V_i$ is nonempty; it is open by continuity of the atlas point map. Density of $D_i$ gives a point of $O_i\cap D_i$, whose image lies in $O\cap|D|$. Hence every nonempty open meets $|D|$, proving density. If $Y$ is empty, take $D=Y$; the same conclusion is vacuous and the empty morphism has both properties by the empty pointwise chart test above. If $X$ is empty, the construction and the locality test also allow empty source charts. No irreducible-component decomposition or finiteness of the cover has been used.

lean.statement: theorem exists_dense_open_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_reduced {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hred : IsReduced Y) (hft : MapIsFiniteType f) : ∃ D : OpenSubspace Y, Dense (pointImage D.val.ι) ∧ ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Limits.pullback f.hom.hom D.val.ι) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ D.val.toFunctor) (h : U ⟶ V), IsEtale a → IsEtale b → a ≫ Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom D.val.ι = yoneda.map h ≫ b → Flat h.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation h.left
